0.text: The process starts when the player begins character creation. Two strands run in parallel: the player brainstorms character names, and at the same time checks for an existing battle.net account. If an account is not found, the player enters account information and confirms it via email before continuing. The player then checks whether a World of Warcraft subscription is active; if it is not, a payment method is selected and either credit card details are entered or bank account data (IBAN and BIC) is provided. With an active subscription in place, the player logs in and selects a realm, race, and class. Once both the brainstorming and the login/selection are completed, the player enters a character name. If the name is not available, the player re-enters a different name until one is available. When an available name is chosen, Blizzard Systems send a confirmation including selfies to the player, who receives it, completing the character confirmation. After dispatching that confirmation, Blizzard Systems wait until an expansion is released; when it is, they send an expansion release message to the player, who receives it, completing the expansion message delivery.

0.text: The process starts when the applicant decides to work and live in Austria, then reviews the visa requirements and determines the visa type (Rot-Weiss-Rot Card), gathers the required documents, obtains Schengen-wide travel health insurance with 30,000 EUR coverage, prepares proof of means and other evidence, and identifies the competent representation office. At this point, the applicant checks whether the documents are complete; if anything is missing, they return to gathering documents until the set is complete. Once complete, the applicant submits the visa application (Type D / Rot-Weiss-Rot Card) and communicates it to the Austrian representation office, where a preliminary check of completeness is performed. The office decides whether additional documents are needed: if so, it requests more documents from the applicant, who then provides the additional documents and sends them back, upon which the office resumes the preliminary check; if not, the office proceeds to assess the application and make a decision. If the decision is a refusal, the office notifies the refusal and the process ends with the visa refused. If the application is approved, the office issues the Rot-Weiss-Rot Card / Type D visa and informs the applicant, who then organizes accommodation (with a communication to the landlord to review the tenant application and negotiate the lease), and opens a bank account (with a communication to the bank to verify identity and open the account). After these arrangements, the applicant decides whether to continue staying in Austria: if not, the process ends with setup complete (living and working in Austria); if yes, the process waits until renewal is due, after which the applicant renews the Rot-Weiss-Rot Card application and submits it again, returning to the submission step and repeating the decision-making cycle.

1.text: The process starts when the applicant begins relocating to Austria. The applicant first checks the requirements to work and live in Austria, after which preparations proceed in parallel along three tracks. On the immigration track, the applicant determines the competent representation office (consulate), collects the required visa documents, and submits the Rot-Weiß-Rot Card application to the consulate; this submission is also sent to the consulate as a communication. The consulate checks the application’s completeness and requirements and decides whether additional documents are needed. If additional documents are needed, the consulate requests them and communicates this request to the applicant, who then provides the additional documents and sends them back to the consulate for another check; this loop continues until no further documents are needed. The consulate then makes a decision on the application: if rejected, the process ends with the application refused; if approved, the consulate issues the Rot-Weiß-Rot Card and notifies the applicant, and this issuance also marks completion of this track for the overall preparation. In parallel on the accommodation track, the applicant initiates the accommodation search and negotiation, engaging the accommodation provider to negotiate terms, and then finalizes the rental agreement. In parallel on the banking track, the applicant compares banks and prepares account documents, applies to open a bank account, and sends the application to the bank for processing. Once the visa is issued, the rental agreement is finalized, and the bank account application step is completed, preparations are considered complete and the applicant enters Austria and starts employment; the consulate’s issuance also triggers the applicant’s entry notification. After entry, the process waits until renewal is due, at which point the applicant renews the Rot-Weiß-Rot Card and decides whether to continue residing in Austria. If continuing, the process concludes in the state of living and working in Austria (representing the continuation of residence and work); if not, the process ends with residency ended.

2.text: The journey starts when the applicant plans to work and live in Austria, checks requirements and eligibility (Rot-Weiss-Rot Card / Schengen), and identifies the competent representation office. From there, the applicant proceeds in parallel to organize accommodation and a bank account: they negotiate accommodation and notify the accommodation provider, which negotiates terms and then confirms the lease agreement back to the applicant, who signs it; at the same time, the applicant initiates the bank account opening and contacts the bank, which receives the request, performs KYC and opens the account, then confirms the opening so the applicant can finalize the setup. Once both accommodation and bank arrangements are in place, the applicant compiles the visa application dossier (forms, passport, photo, insurance, proof of funds, evidence) and submits the application to the Austrian representation, which receives it and checks completeness and visa requirements. If additional documents are needed, the representation requests them from the applicant, who provides the requested items; the representation receives these and rechecks until complete. When the file is complete, the representation decides on the visa; if the outcome is approval, it issues the visa/Rot-Weiss-Rot Card and notifies the applicant, and if the outcome is refusal, it sends a refusal notice to the applicant. The applicant receives the decision and, in any case, the situation advances to living and working in Austria; if the received decision is an approval, the applicant also enters a recurring cycle in which, whenever renewal becomes due, they prepare a renewal dossier and submit the renewal application back to the representation, after which a new decision is received and the cycle can repeat; if the received decision is a refusal, the process ends with the visa refused.

3.text: After deciding to work and live in Austria, the applicant determines the appropriate visa or permit type and the competent Austrian representation, then collects the general required documents by completing the application form, checking that the travel document is valid for at least three months beyond the stay with two empty pages and issued within the last ten years, obtaining a compliant 35x45 mm passport photo, purchasing comprehensive Schengen-wide travel health insurance covering at least €30,000, preparing proof of sufficient means of subsistence and return, gathering other evidence such as hotel reservations, invitations, bookings, return ticket, and employment documentation, and self-checking the absence of grounds for refusal (e.g., residence prohibition or SIS alert). The applicant then contacts the representation in advance to clarify local requirements and submits the application to the competent Austrian representation. The representation checks the application and its own competence and decides whether additional documents are required: if yes, the applicant provides the additional documents and the representation rechecks; if no, the representation proceeds to decide on the application. If the application is refused, the process ends with the application not being granted; if approved, the representation issues the visa or Rot-Weiss-Rot Card as applicable, after which the applicant travels to and enters Austria. Upon arrival, the applicant organizes accommodation and a bank account in parallel; once both are completed, the process proceeds to a point where either the initial setup is considered complete, in which case the process can end with living and working established, and/or periodic renewal is enabled. If periodic renewal is enabled, a renewal timer triggers every defined number of months, prompting the applicant to submit a renewal or extension application that the representation then reviews; if the renewal is not approved, the process ends with the residence or visa not renewed, whereas if it is approved, the cycle returns to the renewal timer for the next period.

The applicant then gathers all visa documents and evidence, determines the competent representation office in line with Schengen/Type D rules, and submits the visa application (Rot-Weiss-Rot Card / Visa D) to that office. The representation office receives and registers the application, verifies the documents and requirements, and assesses whether additional documents are required; if so, it requests them from the applicant, who provides the additional documents as requested and sends them back for verification, after which the verification continues to the decision. The office then decides on visa issuance: if rejected, the applicant receives the rejection decision and the process ends with the visa application rejected; if approved, the office issues the Rot-Weiss-Rot Card or Visa D and notifies the applicant, who then receives the approval decision, travels to Austria, and the process reaches the state where living and working in Austria is possible with a valid visa. From there, the competent authority sets the renewal cadence so that every X months a renewal becomes due; when this occurs, the applicant prepares the renewal application and submits it to the State Police Headquarters, which processes the renewal and decides on it. If the renewal is approved, a renewed permit or card is issued and the next renewal due date is set again; if the renewal is rejected, the process ends with a renewal rejected outcome.

The applicant then organizes accommodation and a bank account in parallel: on the accommodation track, the applicant negotiates with a housing provider, exchanges information to receive suitable options, and once an option is chosen signs the lease or tenancy agreement, with confirmations returned to the applicant; on the banking track, the applicant initiates the bank setup, the bank assesses the application, and the account is opened, with confirmation sent back to the applicant. After both tracks have been completed, the applicant submits the visa/residence application to the representation office. The office verifies competence and takes in the application, the applicant attends an appointment and provides biometrics, and the office checks the application and documents. If additional documents are requested, the office asks for them and the applicant provides them, after which the check resumes; otherwise the case proceeds to a decision. The office prepares and makes a decision: if refused, the process ends with the application refused; if approved, the office issues the visa/permit and notifies the applicant to collect it, after which the applicant collects the visa/permit and is settled in Austria. Following collection, the applicant begins monitoring permit validity at regular intervals. When a renewal becomes due, the applicant prepares renewal documents, submits the renewal application (which also notifies the office to process it), attends a renewal appointment, and the office processes the renewal and decides. If the renewal is refused, the process ends with the application refused; if approved, the renewed permit is issued and the applicant is informed, the renewal is completed, and monitoring resumes for the next cycle.

6.text: The applicant begins by checking the requirements for working and living in Austria, then prepares the required visa documents. Next, the applicant organizes two preparations in parallel: negotiates and organizes accommodation while also organizing and opening a bank account; once both are finished, the applicant determines the visa type and the competent representation office and then submits the visa application (e.g., Rot-Weiss-Rot Card). Upon submission, the application is sent to the Austrian representation office, where the representation process starts with receiving and reviewing the application. The representation decides whether additional documents are required: if yes, it requests additional documents from the applicant; the applicant provides the additional documents when requested and sends them back, after which the representation returns to review the application and repeats the same decision until no further documents are required. When ready to decide, the representation either approves or refuses the application. If approved, the representation issues the visa / Rot-Weiss-Rot Card and notifies the applicant to collect it; the applicant then collects the visa / Rot-Weiss-Rot Card, travels, and enters Austria, after which the process reaches the outcome “visa/permit granted and entry completed.” If refused, the representation notifies the applicant of the refusal, and the process ends with “application or renewal refused.” After the outcome where the visa/permit is granted and entry completed, time passes until renewal is due (every x months), prompting the applicant to apply for permit renewal; the renewal application is sent to the representation, which processes the renewal and decides on it. If the renewal is approved, the representation notifies the applicant, who receives the renewal approval decision and reaches the outcome “residence maintained after renewal.” If the renewal is refused, the representation notifies the applicant, who receives the refusal decision and the process ends with “application or renewal refused.”

The applicant first checks the requirements for working and living in Austria and determines the competent representation office. When the validity period has elapsed, the applicant prepares a renewal application and submits it to the representation office, which reviews the renewal. If the renewal is refused, the process ends with the renewal refused and the stay ending; if approved, the office issues the renewal and informs the applicant, who collects the renewed card or visa. 0.text: The process starts when the DIY repairer begins by entering the smartphone model and the issue; at this point, the information is sent to the online tool’s backend to generate the list of materials, tools, and ordering options. Next, the repairer identifies which items are already available. The work then proceeds in parallel: the repairer requests items from friends while also purchasing the remaining items. As part of requesting items from friends, a request is sent to the friends network, which then provides or sells/loans the requested items. Once both the requests to friends and the purchases are completed, the repairer confirms that all required items have been acquired. Upon this confirmation, a request is sent to the online tool’s backend to obtain repair instructions, and those instructions are then delivered back to the repairer. The repairer performs the repair following the provided instructions. Afterwards, a decision is made: if the repair is successful, the repairer sends a review and/or video, and the process ends with the repair completed; if not, the repairer sends the phone to an expert, notifying the expert service, where the expert repairs the smartphone, and the process ends with the phone sent to the expert.

1.text: The process begins when the user starts and enters the phone model and the issue. Based on this input, the online tool generates lists of required materials, tools, and ordering options. Preparation then proceeds along two concurrent paths: the user contacts friends to borrow or buy items, prompting friends to respond to the request, and at the same time the user purchases any remaining required items. 0.text: The process starts with the parent fetching information about available leave models, then selecting a leave model and collecting the relevant information. Next, the parent proceeds in parallel to notify Social Security and to notify the employer; after the employer has been notified, the employer provides employment information, which the parent gathers. Once both the notification to Social Security and the gathering of the employer’s information are completed, the process waits until the end of the current leave period. The parent then decides whether to extend the leave: if no extension is needed, the process ends with maternity leave completed; if an extension is requested, the parent submits the extension request and then, again in parallel, notifies Social Security of the extension and notifies the employer of the extension. These two extension notifications are synchronized, and the process ends with maternity leave extended. Throughout, the following communications occur: Social Security receives the maternity leave notification and later receives the extension notification; the employer receives the maternity leave notification, then provides employment information back to the parent, and later receives the extension notification.

1.text: The process starts in the E‑Gov Portal when planning maternity leave begins. The portal first gathers information about potential models and sends these to the parent, who reviews the models and makes a selection; the selection is returned to the portal. The portal then asks the parent for the relevant information; the parent provides it, and once received the portal proceeds to perform two actions in parallel: it notifies Social Security and it notifies the company. Social Security receives the maternity leave notification, while the company processes the notification and returns the required company information to the portal. After both the Social Security notification has been sent and the company information has been received, the portal considers the leave established. The portal then requests from the parent a decision on whether to extend the leave; the parent makes this decision and sends it back. If the decision is to extend, the process concludes with the leave extended. Otherwise, the portal returns to request the relevant information from the parent again and repeats the subsequent steps from there until an extension decision eventually leads to extension.

With these details in hand, the portal sends a maternity leave notification to Social Security, which is received as a maternity leave notification by its intake. The portal also issues a second maternity leave notification intended for the company; in the model, this is received as a maternity leave notification by Social Security’s intake. The portal then requests employer information from the company’s HR; HR provides the employment information, and the portal receives it and consolidates the employer information. The process continues until the end of the maternity leave period is reached. At that point, the portal asks the parent whether to extend the maternity leave; the request goes to the parent, who decides and returns the decision, which the portal receives. If no extension is chosen, the case is closed with maternity leave completed. If an extension is chosen, the portal notifies Social Security about the extension (received by Social Security’s intake as an extension notification) and also sends an extension notification intended for the company; in the model, this is received by Social Security’s intake as an extension notification. 0.text: The process starts with the robot receiving the order and immediately asking whether it is a menu or just a burger. If the choice is “menu,” the work splits so that a drink is prepared while, in parallel, the side is determined and prepared: the robot asks whether the side should be fries or wedges and then prepares fries if “fries” is chosen or prepares wedges if “wedges” is chosen. Once both the drink and the chosen side are finished, the robot proceeds to prepare the burger, providing status updates every 30 seconds. If the initial choice is “just burger,” the robot skips the drink and side entirely and goes straight to preparing the burger with the same periodic status updates. In both cases, after the burger is ready, the robot delivers the order via a conveyor belt and the process ends.

1.text: When an order is received, the attendant asks whether it is a menu or just a burger. If it is a menu, the process splits so that the drink is prepared while, in parallel, the customer is asked to choose fries or wedges. Based on that choice, either fries are prepared or wedges are prepared. Once both the drink and the selected side are ready, the flow continues to prepare the burger, providing status updates every 30 seconds. If the customer wants just a burger, the process goes directly to preparing the burger with the same periodic status updates. In either case, after the burger is ready, the order is delivered via a conveyor belt, and the process ends with the order delivered.

2.text: The process starts in the Robotic Burger Seller when an order is received, after which the robot asks the customer whether they want a full menu or just a burger and records the customer’s answer. Based on that choice, if the customer wants a full menu, the robot proceeds with two activities at the same time: it prepares a drink, and it engages the customer to select a side. For the side, the robot asks whether the customer prefers fries or wedges; the customer responds with their choice, the robot records it, and then it prepares fries or prepares wedges accordingly. Once both the drink and the chosen side are ready, the robot continues to prepare the burger, providing status updates every 30 seconds during this step. If the customer chose just a burger earlier, the robot skips the drink and side and goes directly to preparing the burger with the same periodic status updates. In all cases, after the burger is prepared, the robot delivers the order via a conveyor belt and the process ends. The communications with the customer occur twice: first when the robot asks “menu or just burger?” and receives the selection to be recorded, and, only if a menu was chosen, when the robot asks “fries or wedges?” and receives the side selection to be recorded.

3.text: The Customer process starts with the customer placing an order, then choosing between a menu or just a burger; if a menu is selected, the customer then chooses fries or wedges before later receiving the order from the conveyor and finishing; if just a burger is selected, the customer skips the side choice and directly receives the order from the conveyor and finishes. In parallel, the Robot Seller process starts by receiving the order (upon the customer’s placement), asking “Menu or just burger?”, and waiting for the customer’s choice; if a menu is selected, the flow splits so the drink is prepared while the customer is asked “Fries or wedges?”, after which the robot waits for the side choice and then prepares either fries or wedges accordingly; once the drink and the chosen side are both ready, their paths rejoin and the robot proceeds to prepare the burger; if just a burger is selected, the robot skips drink and side preparation and proceeds straight to preparing the burger. While the burger is being prepared, every 30 seconds an enthusiastic status update is sent before continuing with the burger preparation. When the burger is ready, the order is delivered via the conveyor belt to the customer, who receives it, after which both the robot and customer processes end. Communications occur as follows: the customer’s order initiates the robot’s receipt of the order; the robot’s question about menu vs. burger prompts the customer’s choice; the customer’s choice informs the robot’s waiting step; the robot’s question about fries vs. wedges prompts the customer’s side choice; the customer’s side choice informs the robot’s waiting step; finally, the robot’s conveyor delivery notifies the customer to receive the order.

4.text: The process starts when the robot receives an order, then asks whether it should be a menu or just a burger and sends this question to the customer, who chooses accordingly and returns the choice, which the robot records. If the choice is just a burger, the robot proceeds directly to prepare the burger (providing periodic status updates) and then delivers the order via the conveyor belt, after which the order is marked as delivered. If the choice is a menu, the robot starts preparing the drink while, in parallel, asking whether the side should be fries or wedges and sending this question to the customer; the customer selects fries or wedges and sends the selection back, which the robot records before preparing the chosen side (fries or wedges). Once both the drink and the side are ready, they are joined, and the robot then prepares the burger (with periodic status updates) and delivers the complete order via the conveyor belt, after which the order is marked as delivered.

If the customer chose just a burger, the robot skips drink and side and prepares the burger immediately. If the stock is not less than three but is less than five, the cheapest parts are reordered and the stock level is evaluated again. 1.text: When the contract project is initiated, you first query all web shops for availability, price, and lead time, sending these inquiries to the web shops, which process the queries and respond with availability, price, and lead-time details back to you. You then evaluate the offers and create a per-shop order list, choosing the cheapest combination and splitting orders if needed, and place the resulting orders to the selected web shops. On the web-shop side, purchase orders are received and processed, then internally passed on to prepare and ship a parts batch; shipment results in your receiving a parts-batch notification. Upon each batch receipt, you update inventory and decide whether the delivery you just received is the first batch or a subsequent one: if it is the first batch, you start building and then continue to build the product; if it is a subsequent batch, you skip directly to checking stock levels for the single part currently in focus. After building (on the first-batch path) or directly (on the subsequent-batch path), you check stock against thresholds and branch as follows: if stock equals 0, you send a complaint email to your friends (who read it) and then reorder the missing parts from the fastest supplier; if stock is less than 3, you reorder from the fastest supplier; if stock is less than 5, you reorder from the cheapest supplier; otherwise, you do not reorder. In all cases where you reorder, you proceed to the next step; if you did not reorder, you proceed directly. You then decide whether more parts or work remain: if yes, you loop back to await and receive the next parts batch and repeat the same receipt, inventory update, first-batch/subsequent-batch choice, building, and stock-threshold handling; if no, all product builds are complete and the process ends.

The buyer receives a parts batch and decides whether this is the first batch: if it is, production starts building and then checks the stock level for the part; if it is not, the stock level is checked directly. Based on the stock threshold, if the stock is at least 5, the buyer waits for the next batch by returning to receiving another parts batch. If the stock is below 5, a reorder rule is applied: when stock is between 3 and 4 inclusive, the buyer reorders the cheapest parts and then awaits the next batch; when stock is 1 or 2, the buyer reorders with fastest delivery and then awaits the next batch; when stock is 0, a complaint email is sent to friends and the process ends with the complaint sent.

The arrival of the first batch is recorded and triggers Production to build the product with the available parts; any subsequent batch arrivals also trigger further building. After each build step, Inventory Management checks the stock level for the part and decides how to proceed: if nothing is left (stock == 0), a complaint email is written to friends, after which another parts batch is considered received and work continues; if the stock is low (stock < 3), parts are reordered with the fastest option, the purchase orders are placed again and another batch arrives to continue building; if the stock is somewhat low (stock < 5), parts are reordered with the cheapest option, the purchase orders are placed again and another batch arrives to continue building; otherwise, it is assessed whether the project is complete—if it is, the project is completed; if not, another parts batch is awaited and, upon its arrival, building resumes. The Web Shops respond by providing quotes, which are then evaluated to create a per‑shop order list that selects the cheapest options and splits across shops if needed. On receipt, if this is the first batch, building is started; at that point the state “Building in progress” is reached while work proceeds to build the product and then check the stock level for a part. For subsequent batches, the stock level is checked directly. If the stock is exactly 0, a complaint email is sent to friends; this both triggers a fastest reorder and also concludes the process with “Process ended after complaint.” If the stock is greater than 0, it is assessed against thresholds: when it is less than 3, a fastest reorder is placed; when it is 3 or 4, a cheapest reorder is placed; and when it is 5 or more, the team waits for further incoming batches. Any reorder (fastest or cheapest) leads back to receiving batches, and each shipment from the Web Shops results in another batch being received. This cycle of receiving, (if first batch) starting and continuing building, checking stock, and reordering as needed continues while shipments keep arriving. Communications between participants are as follows: the Project Team sends a query to the Web Shops and receives their quotes; it sends orders to the Web Shops, which process them; and the Web Shops ship batches that the Project Team receives.

0.text: The process starts in the Player/Bot domain when the bot initiates and the player first gathers the desired resources and priorities, after which the bot determines dependencies and required tools. If a pickaxe is needed, the bot collects iron ore and crafts a pickaxe; otherwise it proceeds without those steps. Next, if a fishing rod is needed, the bot collects plant fiber and crafts a fishing rod; otherwise it continues directly. The bot then runs the farming routine. While farming, several situations may occur and loop back into farming: upon reaching a milestone, the bot notes the milestone and notifies the player before continuing; if a natural disaster strikes, recovery is performed and farming resumes; and when target updates are triggered, the player updates the target materials list and hands control back to the bot to continue farming. When the farming run is ready to be shared, a decision is made whether to share with friends, allowing one or both of the following: the player brags to selected friends, which is communicated to the friends who receive the brag, and/or materials are sent to friends, which are then received by them. After the chosen sharing actions complete, the process finishes with farming completed.

1.text: The process starts when the player begins by selecting the desired resources and then defining priorities and dependencies. Based on this input, the farming bot generates a farming plan that limits execution to at most ten resources in parallel and proceeds to farm the resources in parallel. While farming, several things can happen: if a natural disaster occurs, the bot pauses to recover from the setback and then resumes farming; when a milestone is reached, the bot sends a notification and then continues farming, which the player receives as a milestone notification; independently, the player can submit a materials update at any time, which is received by the bot, processed to adjust the plan, and applied before looping back into farming. Once farming is complete, the bot proceeds to the sharing options stage (and/or), where the player may choose to brag to selected friends and/or send materials to friends; each chosen option is performed and then returns to the sharing stage, after which the process ends. During these communications, the bot’s milestone notification is delivered to the player, the player’s materials update is delivered to the bot, and any bragging and materials transfers are delivered to the respective friends, who receive the brag and the materials.

2.text: The process begins in the game when the player starts and provides resource preferences, including priorities and dependencies. Based on these inputs, the farming bot computes a dependency plan and batching that allows up to 10 activities to proceed in parallel, then starts farming and proceeds to execute the collection plan, again allowing up to 10 items to be collected in parallel. Once this collection run concludes, the player selects sharing options: they may choose to brag to selected friends and/or send materials to selected friends; each selected option is carried out, and when all chosen options have been completed the process finishes. While farming is underway, several events can influence the flow: if a natural disaster strikes, recovery is performed and the process returns to executing the collection plan; whenever a milestone is reached, a milestone notification is prepared and sent, after which the process returns to executing the collection plan; and if an update to the farming list is requested, the player updates resource preferences and the bot recomputes the plan before continuing. Communications occur as follows: when a milestone is reached, the bot sends a notification to the player; if the player chose to brag, the brag is delivered to friends; and if the player chose to send materials, the materials are delivered to friends.

3.text: The process starts, and the desired resources and their priorities are determined, after which resource dependencies and the required tooling are defined. The farming run is then started and parallel farming is executed for up to 10 resources. After each farming cycle, it is checked whether a milestone has been reached; if so, a notification about the milestone is sent before proceeding, otherwise the process continues without notification. Next, it is checked whether a natural disaster has occurred; if it has, recovery from the setback is carried out, and in any case the process moves on to decide whether to update the materials list. If an update is needed, the materials to be farmed are updated and execution returns to the parallel farming step. If no update is needed, it is then checked whether farming is finished; if it is not, execution returns to parallel farming, and if it is, post‑farming actions are chosen, where bragging to friends and sending materials can be done independently and in combination. The player then decides whether to brag to selected friends; if yes, the player brags and then decides whether to send materials; if no, the process moves directly to the decision about sending materials. If the player chooses to send materials, the materials are sent to selected friends; otherwise the process ends. The farming bot then carries out the farming execution. While this is running, milestones may be reached; when that happens, a milestone notification is issued and execution continues. The player receives this notification and may update the farming list, which sends updated preferences to the bot; upon receiving these preferences, the bot updates the farming targets and resumes execution. After an execution cycle, a check is made for a natural disaster. If one has occurred, a disaster is signaled, the bot recovers from the setback, and farming execution resumes. If no disaster occurred, the player proceeds to sharing: they may choose to brag to selected friends and/or send materials to friends. The corresponding communications are sent to friends, who receive the brag and receive the materials. Once all chosen sharing actions are completed, the process finishes.

7.text: The process begins on two tracks. On the player side, setup starts with identifying the desired resources, then setting priorities and dependencies, and reviewing and confirming these preferences. Once confirmed, this information is sent to the bot to kick off its run. Separately, the bot can also be started directly; it initializes the farming run and begins collecting resources (up to 10 in parallel, respecting the provided priorities and dependencies). During collection, three kinds of situations may occur: if a natural disaster occurs, the bot handles the setback and resumes collecting; if a milestone is reached, the bot notifies the player, after which the player reviews the milestone notification, and the bot continues collecting; if no such event occurs, the bot checks whether there are more resources to collect: if so, it continues collecting, otherwise it finalizes the farming run and signals completion. At any time after the player’s confirmation, the player updates the materials list, which is sent to the bot; upon receiving it, the bot applies the updated farming list. When the bot signals that farming is completed, the player reviews the farming results and then decides how to share outcomes: the player may brag to selected friends and/or send materials to selected friends. Brag messages and materials are delivered to the respective friends, who receive the brag and the materials accordingly; once the chosen sharing actions are done, the player’s process ends.

8.text: The collaboration starts in two places: the player begins by identifying desired resources and priorities, and the farming bot starts by analyzing dependencies to plan which tools are needed. As soon as the player has specified preferences, that information is sent to the bot, which uses it in its analysis. The bot then prepares all required tools at the same time: it crafts an axe, a pickaxe, and a sickle, builds a furnace, and crafts a fishing rod; once all of these are ready, it moves on to gather resources. It then fans out to collect up to ten different resources in parallel (wood, ore, fiber, herbs, fish, gems, metal bars, arrows, potions, and runes). After each individual resource is collected, the bot issues a milestone notification to the player and then continues until all selected resources have been gathered. When collection is complete, the bot checks whether a natural disaster has occurred; if so, it performs recovery from the setback and restarts the resource collection phase, otherwise it informs the player that farming is finished and concludes its work. At any time, the player may send an updated resource list, which the bot receives and uses to re-run its analysis before proceeding. After the player receives the “farming finished” notice, the player selects friends and then carries out post actions at the same time: bragging to the chosen friends and sending them materials. The brag and the materials are delivered to the respective friends, and once these post actions are done, the player’s part of the process ends.

9.text: The process starts in two places. On the player side, it begins when the player defines desired resources and priorities and then reviews and confirms the preferences; at that point the confirmed preferences are sent to the bot. The player then moves into a phase where two tracks run in parallel: one track waits for a farming-complete message, and the other repeatedly receives milestone notifications. Each time a milestone notification arrives, the player decides whether there are more milestones to wait for, whether to request an update to the resource list, or whether they are done waiting; if an update is requested, the player updates the resource list and sends an update request to the bot, then resumes receiving milestones, and this loop continues until the player decides they are done waiting, at which point the waiting/notification tracks rejoin. After that, the player chooses how to share results: they may brag to selected friends and/or send materials, possibly doing either or both; bragging triggers a brag to be received by friends, and sending materials triggers materials to be received by friends. Once these sharing actions conclude, the player’s process ends. In parallel, the bot starts by receiving the player’s preferences and analyzing resource dependencies and priorities. If dependencies are not yet satisfied, the bot crafts the required tools and reanalyzes until they are; once satisfied, it proceeds to farm resources (up to ten in parallel). While farming, it periodically raises milestones, which are sent as notifications to the player, and it guards against issues: if a natural disaster occurs during farming, it recovers from the setback and resumes farming; if an update request from the player arrives during farming, it applies the updated resource list and returns to analysis before continuing. When farming completes, the bot notifies completion and sends the farming-complete message to the player’s waiting track, allowing the player’s parallel phase to finish.

0.text: When an incident occurs (accident or near-miss), the insured person or employee first collects incident details. Based on these details, it is determined whether it was an accident or a near-miss. If it was a near-miss, the employee informs the employer immediately and the near-miss is recorded. If it was an accident, the situation is assessed against the criteria for a covered work accident. If it is not covered as a work accident, the insured party reports the accident to the private insurer immediately in writing, after which the private insurer is notified. If it is a covered work accident, the injury severity is assessed to determine whether there was a fatality or serious injury. In the case of a fatality or serious injury, it is checked whether emergency services have already been notified; if not, the employer reports immediately to the Labour Inspectorate, otherwise the process proceeds directly. Next, the path depends on the participant type: for an insured employee, the employer reports the accident to the accident insurance provider within five days; for a self-employed person, the self-employed reports the accident(s) to the accident insurance provider; for a student or schoolchild, the student or schoolchild reports the accident to the competent directorate, after which the school or university reports the accident to the accident insurance provider within five days in triplicate. In each of these three cases, reporting to the accident insurance provider is completed.

1.text: When an incident or near miss occurs, the details are first captured. The situation is then classified: if it is a near miss, serious risk, or defect, the employer is notified immediately and the process ends. If it is an accident, the incident is assessed to determine whether it qualifies as a work accident. If it does not qualify, it is checked whether the person has private insurance; if yes, the accident is reported to the private insurer immediately in writing, after which it is determined whether there was a fatality; if so, the fatality is reported to the private insurer within three days and the process ends; if not, the process ends. If the person has no private insurance, the process ends. If the accident does qualify as a work accident, two tracks proceed in parallel. On the statutory side, the person category is identified. If the person is an employee, the employer is notified immediately, the employer evaluates the accident’s severity, and it is determined whether there was a fatality or serious injury. If so, it is checked whether emergency services have already been notified; if not, the Labour Inspectorate is notified immediately, then it is determined whether someone was killed or is unable to work for three days or more; if yes, the Accident Insurance Provider is notified within five days and the process ends; if no, the process ends. If emergency services have already been notified, the Labour Inspectorate step is skipped and the determination of whether someone was killed or is unable to work for three or more days is made directly, leading either to notifying the Accident Insurance Provider within five days (if yes) or ending the process (if no). If the person is self-employed, the accident is reported to the Accident Insurance Provider and the process ends. If the person is a student or schoolchild, the accident is reported to the directorate, which then reports to the Accident Insurance Provider in triplicate within five days, after which the process ends. In parallel with the statutory track for qualifying work accidents, it is also checked whether the person has private insurance; if yes, the accident is reported immediately in writing to the private insurer, then it is determined whether there was a fatality; if so, the fatality is reported to the private insurer within three days and the process ends; if not, the process ends. If the person has no private insurance, this path ends immediately.

2.text: When an employee incident is detected, the person first calls emergency services if needed and then assesses the situation against coverage criteria. Based on the incident type, if it is a work accident, the person immediately notifies the employer; if it is a near miss, serious risk, or protection defect, the person informs the employer of that and finishes; if it is not covered as a work accident, the person checks whether private accident insurance applies: with such insurance, the person considers that coverage and prepares a written report before finishing; without such insurance, the person simply finishes. The employer’s process starts upon receiving the incident report from the employee and recording the incident details, after which the employer evaluates whether it is a work accident. If not (near miss/risk/defect), the employer mitigates the risk or repairs protection systems and then finishes. If it is a work accident, the employer determines whether there is a fatality or serious injury; if so, the employer checks whether it has already been reported to emergency services: if not, the employer immediately reports it to the Labour Inspectorate and then proceeds; if it has already been reported to emergency services, the employer proceeds directly to the next check. The employer then evaluates whether the person was killed or is unable to work for at least three days; in that case the employer reports the work accident to the Accident Insurance Provider within five days and then finishes; otherwise the employer finishes. For students or schoolchildren, after assessing coverage, if it is a covered work accident, they report it to the competent directorate; otherwise they check private insurance applicability: with such insurance, they consider that coverage and prepare a written report before finishing; without it, they finish. The Accident Insurance Provider receives accident reports and then finishes, and the Labour Inspectorate receives immediate reports and then finishes; emergency services receive emergency calls and respond, then finish; and a private insurance provider receives written reports (immediately, with fatalities within three days) and then finishes. If so, it is checked whether emergency services have already been notified; if not, the Labour Inspectorate is notified, and in either case the process continues by checking whether there is incapacity to work of at least three days or a fatality. If it is an accident, the reporter assesses work-accident coverage criteria and decides whether it qualifies as a work accident. If it qualifies, the employer is notified immediately (communication to the employer), after which the reporter assesses injury severity and incapacity and performs a severity assessment: in case of fatality or serious injury, the reporter reports the fatal/serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate (communication to the Labour Inspectorate) and then determines the reporter category; in case of incapacity of at least three days, the reporter proceeds directly to determining the reporter category; in case of a minor injury (less than three days), the reporter also proceeds to determining the reporter category. 0.text: The process starts with the applicant reporting their job applications. This report is sent to the e‑government agency, which processes it and then generates and sends job offers back to the applicant. The applicant reviews the offers and submits a job application, which is sent to the company. The company confirms receipt of the application and informs the agency, which (based on these inputs) continues its processing as needed. The applicant and the company then negotiate a job interview through an exchange: the applicant proposes options and the company responds, and this back‑and‑forth continues until agreement. The company proceeds to offer employment and informs the applicant, who then enters a probation phase. Afterward, the applicant rates the company. If the job does not become permanent, the applicant returns to reporting job applications and the cycle can repeat; if it does become permanent, the applicant’s rating is considered. If this rating is C or less, the applicant goes back to reviewing job offers; otherwise, the process concludes. In parallel on the company side, after confirming receipt the company rates the application, conducts the interview negotiation as above, and after offering employment later rates the employee. The company’s ratings are sent to the agency, which stores the reviews, waits one year, then makes the reviews visible and notifies applicants so they can view the company reviews.

1.text: The process starts with the applicant writing job applications and then reporting those applications to the job agency. Each application is also sent to the company, which confirms receipt and notifies the applicant accordingly. The agency processes the applicant’s report and returns job offers for the applicant to review. The company, upon receiving an application, confirms receipt, evaluates the application, decides whether to invite the applicant to an interview, and, if so, proposes the interview to the applicant, who then negotiates it; if the company decides not to invite, it re-evaluates the application. After reviewing offers, the applicant negotiates an interview and then checks whether an employment offer has arrived: if no offer is received, the applicant returns to writing new applications; if an offer is received, the company issues the offer and the applicant accepts it. The applicant then enters a probation phase after which it is determined whether the job becomes permanent: if it does not, the applicant returns to writing applications; if it does, the applicant rates the company, waits one year for the review to become visible, then views the company’s reviews. Based on the applicant’s own rating, if the rating is C or less the applicant returns to reviewing job offers; otherwise, the process ends. Independently on the company side after making an offer, the company rates the applicant.

2.text: The process starts with the applicant reporting job applications, which are sent to the employment agency. The agency processes these reports, generates job offers, and sends them to the applicant for review. The applicant reviews the offers and negotiates a job interview with the company; this triggers the company’s interview to be conducted if an interview was agreed, otherwise the company proceeds directly to decide. On the company side, they first confirm receipt of the application and rate it, then determine whether an interview has been negotiated; if so, they conduct the interview before making a hiring decision; if not, they make the decision immediately. If the decision is not to hire, the process ends on the company side as not hired/not permanent. If the decision is to hire, the company makes a job offer and sends it to the applicant; the applicant receives the job offer and enters a probation phase. While the applicant is in probation, the company evaluates the probation outcome, rates the candidate, and decides whether the job becomes permanent; if not, the process ends on the company side as not hired/not permanent, and if yes, the company confirms the permanent job and notifies the applicant, who then receives the permanent job decision. After receiving this decision, the applicant assesses whether their own company rating is C or less: if so, they return to reviewing job offers; otherwise, the process ends for the applicant with the permanent job. Independently, the applicant’s company rating and the company’s candidate rating are both sent to the agency, which publishes company reviews; publication can also be triggered once one year has elapsed. The published reviews are then made available to the applicant for viewing.

3.text: The process starts with the applicant reporting their job applications, which the employment agency receives. The applicant then receives job offers sent by the agency and proceeds to submit a chosen application to a company; the company receives it, confirms receipt and rates the application, prompting the applicant to negotiate and schedule an interview. Both sides coordinate interview scheduling, after which the company makes a job offer and sends it to the applicant, who receives it. If no offer is actually received, the applicant returns to reporting applications and the cycle repeats. If an offer is received, the applicant enters a probation phase and rates the company; in parallel, after a one-year wait the applicant views company reviews. Next, if the job does not become permanent, the applicant resumes reporting applications. If it does become permanent, and if the applicant’s rating is C or less, the applicant continues to receive job offers from the agency without needing to report and can submit applications directly from those offers; otherwise, the process ends.

4.text: The job search starts with the applicant receiving job offers, then sending a job application to a company and reporting the applications to the employment agency. The report is communicated to the agency, which generates job offers based on the applications and sends these offers back to the applicant; this also feeds a loop that keeps the applicant receiving new offers. The application sent to the company is communicated to the company, which confirms receipt and rates the application, and this confirmation and rating are sent back to the applicant. The company then decides whether an interview is needed: if yes, it proposes a job interview to the applicant, who negotiates the interview with the company; otherwise the process moves directly to deciding whether to hire the applicant. If the company decides not to hire, the flow returns to the applicant receiving job offers. If the company decides to hire, it sends a job offer to the applicant, who accepts the offer and starts a probation period; this acceptance is also communicated back to the company. After the probation phase, the process branches so that the applicant rates the company while the company rates the applicant, and these are joined before waiting until the reviews are visible after one year at the agency. The agency then publishes company reviews to applicants and decides whether the job becomes permanent: if not, the flow returns to the applicant receiving job offers; if it does, the applicant’s rating is checked—if it is above C, the process ends with a permanent job accepted; otherwise, it ends with the applicant continuing to receive offers only.

5.text: The process starts with the applicant and proceeds as follows: after the start, the applicant submits job applications and then reports these applications to the agency. This report is sent to the agency, where the applications are recorded, job offers are generated, and the offers are sent back to the applicant. In parallel, each submitted application is conveyed to the company, which confirms receipt, rates the application, arranges an interview, and later decides whether to hire; the interview negotiation from the applicant is communicated to the company to support arranging the interview, and the company’s hiring decision is communicated back to the applicant. The applicant, upon receiving job offers, reviews them, negotiates an interview, and then receives the employment decision. If not hired, the applicant returns to submitting applications and repeats the cycle. If hired, the applicant works through a probation phase, then rates the company; this review is sent to the agency, which acknowledges it and, after one year has elapsed, publishes the review. After rating the company, the applicant receives the permanence decision from the company (issued after the company rates the applicant and decides on permanence following probation). If the job does not become permanent, the applicant returns to submitting applications. If it does become permanent, the applicant proceeds to a final check based on the applicant’s rating: if the rating is C or less, the applicant returns to reviewing job offers; otherwise, the process ends.

6.text: The process starts when a job applicant begins a job search and reports the applications they have sent; this report is communicated to the job agency, which then issues job offers based on those applications and prompts the applicant to submit a job application. The submitted application is communicated to the company, which confirms receipt and rates the application, after which the applicant and the company negotiate a job interview. A decision is then made on whether the applicant is hired: if not, the search continues and the process ends; if hired, the company makes an employment offer, which is communicated to the applicant, who then enters and completes a probation phase. After probation, two ratings proceed in parallel: the applicant rates the company, and the company rates the applicant; once both ratings are completed, the flow splits again so that, on one branch, a decision is made on whether the job becomes permanent, while on the other, after one year passes, the agency publishes the company reviews to applicants and the flow rejoins, returning to the point where the permanence decision is evaluated. From the permanence decision, either the evaluation of the applicant’s rating is performed or the agency is instructed to continue sending job offers based on applications. If the applicant’s rating is evaluated, a further decision routes either to the overall process end or to a track where the applicant receives job offers without having to report applications, which then concludes with the continuation of offers without reporting.

7.text: The process starts when the job seeker begins job seeking and submits job applications to companies, sending each application to the company, which in turn confirms receipt. The applicant then reports the submitted applications to the employment agency, which uses these inputs (and also the companies’ later application ratings) to generate job offers; from there the agency waits one year before publishing company reviews and, when it later receives the company’s post‑probation applicant ratings, uses them in those publications. The applicant proceeds to review the received job offers and negotiates a job interview with the company; this negotiation is coordinated with the company’s interview scheduling through mutual communications. If an interview is successfully negotiated, the applicant attends it, after which the company evaluates whether it wants to hire: if not, the company process ends; if yes, the company sends a job offer to the applicant, who receives it and then works during a probation phase. During this period and after it, the company rates the applicant and decides on permanent employment, after which the company’s process ends. On the applicant side, after probation the applicant rates the company and then receives the permanence decision. If the job becomes permanent and the applicant’s own rating of the company is better than C, the applicant’s process ends. If the job does not become permanent, the applicant returns to submitting new applications and repeats the reporting and offer review steps. If the job does become permanent but the applicant’s rating of the company is C or less, the applicant continues to review received job offers (skipping the reporting step) while remaining in the process; if instead that rating is better than C, the applicant’s process ends. Throughout, the company rates applications it receives and conducts the interview; its application rating is also provided to the agency to help generate offers.

8.text: The process starts when the job applicant begins the job search, writes job applications, and then regularly reports these applications. The reports are received by the e-government job agency, which generates job offers based on the reported applications and sends those offers back to the applicant. The applicant receives the offers and then awaits an interview invitation from a company. Within the company, applications are first confirmed and rated; the company then decides whether to invite the applicant to an interview. If an invitation is issued, the invitation is communicated to the applicant, who proceeds to negotiate the interview and, in turn, coordinates this negotiation with the company. After the negotiation, the company hires the candidate into a probation phase and communicates a hiring offer to the applicant, who then enters probation. The company later decides on permanent employment and communicates its decision to the applicant. If the job becomes permanent, the applicant rates the company; if that rating is above C, the process ends with a permanent job accepted and a positive rating. If the rating is C or less, the applicant returns to receiving offers, where future offers may also be influenced by company reviews published later. If the job does not become permanent, the applicant returns to writing applications and repeats the reporting and offer cycle. On the company side, when deciding on permanence, if the decision is to make the role permanent, the company rates the applicant, waits one year for visibility, and then publishes company reviews, which are also made available to the applicant alongside incoming offers. If the company decides against permanence, it returns to confirming receipt and rating applications, potentially restarting its interview decision cycle.

9.text: The process begins with the job seeker starting, writing job applications, submitting them to companies, and then reporting the submissions to the employment agency. Based on that report, the agency receives the data, generates job offers, and sends those offers back to the job seeker, who then reviews the received job offers and may loop back to write more applications. In parallel on the company side, after receiving applications, the company confirms receipt, evaluates each application, and decides whether an interview has been negotiated; if so, it conducts an interview and then decides whether it wants to hire, otherwise it goes straight to that hiring decision. When the company decides to hire, this outcome is communicated to the job seeker, who then enters a probation phase and proceeds to a decision point on whether the job becomes permanent; if it does not, the job seeker returns to writing applications, and if it does, the job seeker rates the company. If that rating is above C, the process ends; if the rating is C or less, the job seeker returns to reviewing job offers. Independently, after the company has rated the applicant, one year elapses, prompting the job seeker to view company reviews and then return to reviewing job offers.

0.text: At the manufacturer, the process starts by recording the customer’s properties, after which the ordering of parts is launched in parallel: the guide bar is ordered and then received, the chain is ordered and then received, the power unit is ordered and then received, the housing is ordered and then received, and the electronics are ordered and then received; only when all five parts have been received does the manufacturer proceed to a manual inspection of all parts. Following the inspection, production updates are sent to the customer, the first chainsaw is assembled, and it is shipped to the customer; upon shipping, the customer receives the first chainsaw. The manufacturer then awaits the customer’s acceptance decision; if the prototype is accepted, the remaining chainsaws are produced and the order is fulfilled, whereas if it is not accepted the process ends with the prototype not accepted. On the customer side, the process starts with providing the chainsaw properties to the manufacturer, then receiving the production updates, receiving the first chainsaw, evaluating the first chainsaw, and sending the acceptance decision back to the manufacturer, after which the customer process ends.

1.text: The process starts for the manufacturer when the customer provides chainsaw requirements, which are sent to and received by Customer Service. The manufacturer then places orders for parts with three sources in parallel and, as each source delivers, the corresponding delivery is received; once all three deliveries have arrived, all parts are inspected manually. After the inspection, two activities proceed at the same time: the first chainsaw is assembled while production updates are sent to the customer. When both the assembly and the updates are completed, the first saw is shipped to the customer. On the customer side, after providing requirements, the customer receives the production updates, then receives and evaluates the first saw, and sends an approval decision back. The manufacturer receives this decision; if the first saw is approved, the remaining order is produced and the process concludes with the order fulfilled. If it is rejected, production is stopped.

2.text: At the manufacturer, the work starts when an order with specifications arrives: parts are ordered from Source A, Source B, and Source C in parallel, and only once all three orders are placed does the process continue to receiving the deliveries. The deliveries are received and the parts are inspected, after which the first chainsaw is assembled. A production update is then sent to the customer, followed by shipment of the first saw, and the manufacturer awaits the customer’s decision. On the customer side, engagement begins separately; the production update is received, then the delivered first saw is evaluated, and an approval decision is sent back to the manufacturer. Upon receiving this decision, the manufacturer determines whether the customer likes the first saw: if so, the remaining order is produced and the order is completed; otherwise, the order is stopped. The communications between the parties are: the production update sent by the manufacturer is received by the customer; the first saw sent by the manufacturer triggers the customer’s evaluation; and the customer’s approval decision is sent back to the manufacturer to proceed or stop.

3.text: The process starts at the manufacturer when production is initiated and the customer provides chainsaw specifications to the manufacturer, who captures these specifications. The work then branches into five concurrent orders: guide bar, chain, power unit (electric or motor), housing, and accessories. For each of these, the manufacturer places the order and sends it to the suppliers, who process the part orders and ship the corresponding parts back; the manufacturer then receives each part in turn (guide bar, chain, power unit, housing, accessories). Once all five parts have been received and come together, the manufacturer inspects all parts. After the inspection, two activities run in parallel: the manufacturer assembles the first chainsaw and also sends production updates to the customer, which the customer receives. When both the assembly and the updates are completed, the manufacturer ships the first chainsaw to the customer, who then reviews it; the customer’s review is returned to the manufacturer as feedback. Based on the feedback, if the customer likes the first chainsaw, the manufacturer produces the remaining chainsaws and the order is fulfilled. If the customer rejects it, the manufacturer closes the order without further production, and the order is closed after rejection.
